claim: During vertebrate embryogenesis, dorsal-ventral patterning is controlled by the BMP/Chordin activator/inhibitor system.
source: During vertebrate embryogenesis, dorsal-ventral patterning is controlled by the BMP/Chordin activator/inhibitor system.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in developmental biology supported by extensive literature.

claim: BMP induces ventral fates.
source: BMP induces ventral fates, whereas Chordin inhibits BMP signaling on the dorsal side.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of developmental biology.

claim: Chordin inhibits BMP signaling on the dorsal side.
source: BMP induces ventral fates, whereas Chordin inhibits BMP signaling on the dorsal side.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of developmental biology.

claim: BMP2b and Chordin diffuse and rapidly form extracellular protein gradients.
source: We found that BMP2b and Chordin diffuse and rapidly form extracellular protein gradients
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F-I and Videos 7-8, where fluorescently tagged BMP2b and Chordin are shown to diffuse and form gradients.

claim: Chordin does not modulate the diffusivity or distribution of BMP2b.
source: Chordin does not modulate the diffusivity or distribution of BMP2b
evidence: This is supported by FRAP data in Figure 4G showing no significant change in BMP2b diffusivity with Chordin overexpression, and by double transplantation experiments in Figure 5.

claim: Chordin is not required to establish peak levels of BMP signaling.
source: Chordin is not required to establish peak levels of BMP signaling.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2F-H showing that BMP signaling on the ventral side is not significantly affected in chordin mutants.

claim: The findings challenge current self-regulating reaction-diffusion and shuttling models.
source: Our findings challenge current self-regulating reaction-diffusion and shuttling models
evidence: This is based on inference from the experimental data that contradict key assumptions of Models 4 and 5.

claim: The findings provide support for a graded source-sink mechanism underlying zebrafish dorsal-ventral patterning.
source: provide support for a graded source-sink mechanism underlying zebrafish dorsal-ventral patterning.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data being most consistent with Model 1 predictions.

claim: The dorsal-ventral axis is one of the earliest coordinate systems established during animal development.
source: The dorsal-ventral axis is one of the earliest coordinate systems established during animal development and divides the embryo into dorsal (back) and ventral (belly) territories.
evidence: This is established knowledge in developmental biology.

claim: The dorsal-ventral axis divides the embryo into dorsal (back) and ventral (belly) territories.
source: The dorsal-ventral axis is one of the earliest coordinate systems established during animal development and divides the embryo into dorsal (back) and ventral (belly) territories.
evidence: This is established knowledge in developmental biology.

claim: The dorsal-ventral axis forms under the influence of the BMP/Chordin patterning system.
source: This axis forms under the influence of the BMP/Chordin patterning system.
evidence: This is established knowledge in developmental biology.

claim: The activator BMP induces the formation of ventral tissues.
source: The activator BMP induces the formation of ventral tissues, and BMP signaling is antagonized on the dorsal side by the inhibitor Chordin.
evidence: This is established knowledge in developmental biology.

claim: BMP signaling is antagonized on the dorsal side by the inhibitor Chordin.
source: The activator BMP induces the formation of ventral tissues, and BMP signaling is antagonized on the dorsal side by the inhibitor Chordin.
evidence: This is established knowledge in developmental biology.

claim: Initially nearly uniform bmp expression refines to a ventrally biased gradient over time.
source: initially nearly uniform bmp expression refines to a ventrally biased gradient over time (Ramel and Hill, 2013; Zinski et al., 2017)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: chd expression is restricted to the dorsal region.
source: chd expression is restricted to the dorsal region (Miller-Bertoglio et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: BMP signaling activity rapidly shifts from a low-level near-uniform distribution to a gradient with peak levels on the ventral side over approximately 3 hr during early zebrafish development.
source: Over the course of approximately 3 hr during early zebrafish development, BMP signaling rapidly shifts from a low-level near-uniform distribution to a gradient with peak levels on the ventral side (Figure 1A+B, Videos 1–5) (Tucker et al., 2008)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A+B and Videos 1-5, as well as a citation to Tucker et al., 2008.

claim: The measured pSmad1/5/9 gradient formation kinetics are consistent with Models 1, 2, 4, and 5.
source: Our measurements are consistent with the gradient kinetics predicted by Models 1, 2, 4, and 5
evidence: This is based on comparison of experimental data in Figure 1B with simulations in Figure 1C-G.

claim: The dynamics predicted by Model 3 do not resemble the experimentally observed pSmad1/5/9 distributions.
source: whereas the dynamics predicted by Model 3 do not resemble the experimentally observed distributions.
evidence: This is based on comparison of experimental data in Figure 1B with simulations in Figure 1E.

claim: In the absence of Chordin, BMP signaling is increased in dorso-lateral domains in chordin−/− mutants compared to wild type embryos.
source: BMP signaling was increased in dorso-lateral domains in chordin−/− mutants compared to wild type embryos
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F-H.

claim: BMP signaling on the ventral side is not significantly affected in chordin−/− mutants.
source: but BMP signaling on the ventral side was not significantly affected (Figure 2F–H)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F-H.

claim: The BMP signaling distribution in chordin mutants is consistent with predictions from Models 1-3.
source: consistent with the predictions from Models 1–3 and observations in Xenopus and zebrafish embryos (Plouhinec et al., 2013; Zinski et al., 2017)
evidence: This is based on comparison of experimental data with model predictions and citations to previous studies.

claim: The BMP signaling distribution in chordin mutants is not consistent with predictions from Models 4 and 5.
source: but not with the BMP signaling distributions predicted by Models 4 and 5 (Table 1).
evidence: This is based on comparison of experimental data with model predictions shown in Table 1.

claim: BMP2b mutants (swr−/−) are normally severely dorsalized.
source: BMP2b mutants (swr−/−, which are normally severely dorsalized [Kishimoto et al., 1997])
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kishimoto et al., 1997.

claim: BMP2b mutants can be rescued by injection of mRNA encoding BMP2b-Dendra2 or BMP2b-sfGFP at levels equivalent to untagged BMP2b.
source: BMP2b mutants (swr−/−, which are normally severely dorsalized [Kishimoto et al., 1997]) can be rescued by injection of mRNA encoding BMP2b-Dendra2 or BMP2b-sfGFP at levels equivalent to untagged BMP2b (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Both BMP2b-sfGFP and Chordin-sfGFP are secreted and diffuse in the extracellular space.
source: Strikingly, both BMP2b-sfGFP and Chordin-sfGFP are secreted and diffuse in the extracellular space (Figure 3F+G, Videos 7+8)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F+G and Videos 7+8.

claim: The observation that BMP2b diffuses contrasts with the proposal of Model 2 that only Chordin – but not BMP – diffuses.
source: in contrast to the proposal of Model 2 that only Chordin – but not BMP – diffuses (Ramel and Hill, 2013) (Table 1)
evidence: This is based on comparison of experimental observations with Model 2 assumptions and a citation.

claim: The observation that BMP2b diffuses contrasts with the absence of long-range BMP4 signaling in Xenopus.
source: and the absence of long-range BMP4 signaling in Xenopus (Jones et al., 1996).
evidence: This is based on comparison of experimental observations with a previous study cited.

claim: Both BMP2b-sfGFP and Chordin-sfGFP rapidly establish concentration gradients over the course of one hour.
source: Both BMP2b-sfGFP and Chordin-sfGFP rapidly establish concentration gradients over the course of one hour (Figure 3H+I)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3H+I.

claim: The rapid gradient formation is consistent with the rapid patterning of the dorsal-ventral axis during zebrafish development.
source: consistent with the rapid patterning of the dorsal-ventral axis during zebrafish development.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of gradient formation kinetics with developmental timing.

claim: The gradient formed by Chordin-sfGFP has a moderately longer range than the one formed by BMP2b-sfGFP.
source: The gradient formed by Chordin-sfGFP has a moderately longer range than the one formed by BMP2b-sfGFP.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3H+I.

claim: 60 min post-transplantation the BMP2b-sfGFP signal drops to 50% of the maximal concentration at a distance of 30–40 µm.
source: For example, 60 min post-transplantation the BMP2b-sfGFP signal drops to 50% of the maximal concentration at a distance of 30–40 µm
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: 60 min post-transplantation the Chordin-sfGFP gradient reaches 50% of its maximal concentration at a distance of 50–60 µm from the source boundary.
source: whereas the gradient formed by Chordin-sfGFP reaches 50% of its maximal concentration at a distance of 50–60 µm from the source boundary at this time point (Figure 3H+I).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Differences in diffusivity or stability could account for the differences in BMP2b and Chordin gradient ranges.
source: This suggests that stability or diffusivity might differ between these proteins (Müller and Schier, 2011; Müller et al., 2013).
evidence: This is inferred from the observed differences in gradient ranges and supported by citations.

claim: Models 3 and 5 assume that BMP is more stable than Chordin.
source: Importantly, Models 3 and 5 assume that BMP is more stable than Chordin, whereas the other models assume either similar or unconstrained stabilities (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Table 1.

claim: BMP2b-Dendra2 has a clearance rate constant of k1 = (8.9 ± 0.1) × 10−5/s (half-life 130 min).
source: For BMP2b-Dendra2, we found a clearance rate constant of k1 = (8.9 ± 0.1) × 10−5/s (half-life 130 min, Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by FDAP experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Chordin-Dendra2 has a clearance rate constant of k1 = (9.6 ± 0.3) × 10−5/s (half-life 120 min).
source: For Chordin-Dendra2, we measured a similar clearance rate constant of k1 = (9.6 ± 0.3) × 10−5/s (half-life 120 min, Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by FDAP experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The similar clearance rate constants of BMP2b and Chordin suggest that differential protein stabilities cannot account for the different protein distributions.
source: The similar clearance rate constants suggest that differential protein stabilities cannot account for the different protein distributions of BMP2b and Chordin.
evidence: This is inferred from the measured clearance rate constants.

claim: The measured clearance rate constants are inconsistent with the differential protein stabilities predicted by Models 3 and 5.
source: Importantly, these results are inconsistent with the differential protein stabilities predicted by Models 3 and 5 (Table 1).
evidence: This is based on comparison of measured values with model predictions shown in Table 1.

claim: BMP2b-Dendra2 has an effective diffusion coefficient of 2.0 ± 0.4 µm2/s.
source: We found effective diffusion coefficients of 2–3 µm2/s for BMPs (BMP2b-Dendra2: 2.0 ± 0.4 µm2/s
evidence: This is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 4C and 4E.

claim: BMP2b-sfGFP has an effective diffusion coefficient of 2.6 ± 0.7 µm2/s.
source: BMP2b-sfGFP: 2.6 ± 0.7 µm2/s (similar to [Zinski et al., 2017])
evidence: This is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 4E and a citation to a previous study.

claim: Chordin-Dendra2 has an effective diffusion coefficient of 6.0 ± 0.7 µm2/s.
source: and of 6–7 µm2/s for Chordin (Chordin-Dendra2: 6.0 ± 0.7 µm2/s
evidence: This is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 4D and 4E.

claim: Chordin-sfGFP has an effective diffusion coefficient of 7.3 ± 3.9 µm2/s.
source: Chordin-sfGFP: 7.3 ± 3.9 µm2/s)
evidence: This is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Slight differences in diffusivities could underlie the differences in BMP2b and Chordin protein distributions.
source: indicating that slight differences in diffusivities could underlie the differences in protein distributions.
evidence: This is inferred from the measured diffusion coefficients.

claim: The measured diffusion coefficients are most consistent with Models 1 and 4.
source: The measured diffusion coefficients are most consistent with Models 1 and 4, which assume either similarly low diffusivities (Model 4) or that BMP has a moderately lower diffusion coefficient than Chordin (Model 1, Table 1).
evidence: This is based on comparison of measured values with model assumptions shown in Table 1.

claim: BMP2b-sfGFP is mobile in vivo.
source: As observed in the BMP2b-sfGFP gradient formation experiment (Figure 3F–I), our FRAP data demonstrate that BMP2b-sfGFP is mobile in vivo, inconsistent with Model 2.
evidence: This is supported by FRAP data and gradient formation experiments.

claim: BMP2b-sfGFP has a free diffusion coefficient of Df = 46 ± 1 µm2/s measured by FCS.
source: local diffusion measurements in very small extracellular volumes far away from cell surfaces using Fluorescence Correlation Spectroscopy (FCS) assays showed that BMP2b-sfGFP (free diffusion coefficient: Df = 46 ± 1 µm2/s)
evidence: This is supported by FCS experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Chordin-sfGFP has a free diffusion coefficient of Df = 59 ± 2 µm2/s measured by FCS.
source: and Chordin-sfGFP (free diffusion coefficient: Df = 59 ± 2 µm2/s) are highly mobile over short spatial and temporal scales (Figure 4F)
evidence: This is supported by FCS experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: BMP2b-sfGFP and Chordin-sfGFP diffusivities are reduced at the global scale when they move across a field of cells compared to local scales.
source: whereas their diffusivities are reduced at the global scale when they move across a field of cells (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of FCS (local) and FRAP (global) measurements.

claim: The difference between effective diffusivities (measured by FRAP) and local diffusivities (measured by FCS) is hypothesized to be due to binding to immobile extracellular molecules.
source: We hypothesize that the difference between effective diffusivities (measured by FRAP) and local diffusivities (measured by FCS) is due to binding to immobile extracellular molecules, which could serve as diffusion regulators that hinder the mobility of BMP2b and Chordin, similar to what has been proposed for other developmental signals such as Nodal and FGF (Müller et al., 2012; Müller et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on inference from the data and supported by citations to similar phenomena.

claim: Model 3 postulates diffusivities of ADMP and Sizzled equivalent to BMP and Chordin.
source: Model 3 postulates diffusivities of ADMP and Sizzled equivalent to BMP and Chordin, whereas Model 4 requires approximately 25-fold higher diffusivities of ADMP and Sizzled compared to BMP and Chordin (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Table 1.

claim: Model 4 requires approximately 25-fold higher diffusivities of ADMP and Sizzled compared to BMP and Chordin.
source: Model 3 postulates diffusivities of ADMP and Sizzled equivalent to BMP and Chordin, whereas Model 4 requires approximately 25-fold higher diffusivities of ADMP and Sizzled compared to BMP and Chordin (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Table 1.

claim: Sizzled-sfGFP has an effective diffusion coefficient of 9.7 ± 3.2 µm2/s.
source: Using FRAP, we measured an effective diffusion coefficient of 9.7 ± 3.2 µm2/s for Sizzled-sfGFP (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The measured Sizzled diffusion coefficient is consistent with Model 3.
source: This measurement is consistent with Model 3, but not Model 4, the latter of which requires much higher Sizzled mobility (Table 1).
evidence: This is based on comparison of measured values with model predictions shown in Table 1.

claim: The measured Sizzled diffusion coefficient is not consistent with Model 4.
source: This measurement is consistent with Model 3, but not Model 4, the latter of which requires much higher Sizzled mobility (Table 1).
evidence: This is based on comparison of measured values with model predictions shown in Table 1.

claim: Model 3 parameterized with measured diffusion coefficients can form ventral-dorsal gradients over relevant time scales.
source: When parameterized with these measured diffusion coefficients and over a ~100-fold range of ADMP diffusion coefficients, Model 3 can form ventral-dorsal gradients over relevant time scales (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F–J)
evidence: This is supported by simulations shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F–J.

claim: The kinetics of gradient formation in Model 3 with measured parameters do not reflect the measurements of pSmad1/5/9 distribution profiles.
source: but the kinetics of gradient formation do not reflect the measurements of pSmad1/5/9 distribution profiles in Figure 1A+B.
evidence: This is based on comparison of simulations with experimental data.

claim: The relatively minor difference between BMP/Chordin and Sizzled diffusivity is not compatible with the 25-fold differential required for Model 4.
source: Moreover, the relatively minor difference between BMP/Chordin and Sizzled diffusivity is not compatible with the 25-fold differential required for Model 4 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1K–P).
evidence: This is based on comparison of measured values with model requirements and simulations shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1K–P.

claim: Model 5 (Shuttling) postulates that highly diffusive Chordin enhances the mobility of poorly diffusive BMPs.
source: Model 5 (Shuttling) postulates that highly diffusive Chordin enhances the mobility of poorly diffusive BMPs (Ben-Zvi et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: In embryos overexpressing Chordin, there was no significant change in the effective diffusivity of fluorescently tagged BMP2b compared to embryos that did not overexpress Chordin.
source: In embryos overexpressing Chordin, we did not observe a significant change in the effective diffusivity of fluorescently tagged BMP2b compared to embryos that did not overexpress Chordin (BMP2b-Dendra2 + Chordin: 2.2 ± 0.2 µm2/s; BMP2b-sfGFP + Chordin: 2.8 ± 0.7 µm2/s; Figure 4G).
evidence: This is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The ability of Chordin to enhance the diffusivity of BMP is not supported by FRAP data.
source: The ability of Chordin to enhance the diffusivity of BMP, a major tenet of Model 5, is therefore not supported by FRAP data.
evidence: This is inferred from the FRAP data showing no effect of Chordin on BMP diffusivity.

claim: Model 5 predicts that Chordin alters the distribution of BMP protein.
source: Model 5 also predicts that Chordin alters the distribution of BMP protein.
evidence: This is stated as a prediction of Model 5.

claim: BMP2b-sfGFP gradients tend to be slightly steeper in the presence of a neighboring Chordin-expressing clone compared to a non-Chordin-expressing clone.
source: Although BMP2b-sfGFP gradients tend to be slightly steeper in the presence of a neighboring Chordin-expressing clone compared to a non-Chordin-expressing clone (Figure 5D)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The minor change in BMP2b-sfGFP gradient steepness in the presence of Chordin is unlikely to account for the formation of a ventral peak in BMP signaling during the short time required to complete dorsal-ventral patterning.
source: this minor change is unlikely to account for the formation of a ventral peak in BMP signaling during the short time (hours) required to complete dorsal-ventral patterning (Figure 1A+B).
evidence: This is inferred from the magnitude of the observed effect and the time scales involved.

claim: Simulations of adjacent BMP and Chordin clones using measured diffusion coefficients and half-lives failed to show significant redistribution of BMP.
source: We also failed to observe significant redistribution of BMP in simulations of adjacent BMP and Chordin clones using our measured diffusion coefficients and half-lives (Figure 5E+F).
evidence: This is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 5E+F.

claim: Shuttling of BMP2b by Chordin is not relevant for the early aspects of dorsal-ventral patterning in zebrafish embryos.
source: This suggests that shuttling of BMP2b by Chordin is not relevant for the early aspects of dorsal-ventral patterning in zebrafish embryos.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental and simulation data showing no significant shuttling effect.

claim: Chordin does not play an active role in generating BMP signaling peaks, but only globally inhibits BMP.
source: First, Chordin does not play an active role in generating BMP signaling peaks, but only globally inhibits BMP (Figure 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: BMP2b and Chordin both diffuse in the extracellular space.
source: Second, BMP2b and Chordin both diffuse in the extracellular space (Figure 3F–I)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F–I.

claim: Fluorescently tagged BMP2b and Chordin have similarly high local diffusivities.
source: Third, fluorescently tagged BMP2b and Chordin have similarly high local diffusivities (Figure 4F)
evidence: This is supported by FCS experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: On a global scale BMP2b and Chordin move much more slowly through the embryo than at local scales.
source: but on a global scale they move much more slowly through the embryo (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The experimental findings rule out Models 2, 3, and 5.
source: These findings rule out Models 2, 3, and 5, but are consistent with Models 1 and 4.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of experimental data with model predictions.

claim: The experimental findings are consistent with Models 1 and 4.
source: These findings rule out Models 2, 3, and 5, but are consistent with Models 1 and 4.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of experimental data with model predictions.

claim: Chordin does not significantly affect BMP2b diffusion or protein distribution in zebrafish embryos.
source: Fourth, Chordin does not significantly affect BMP2b diffusion or protein distribution in zebrafish embryos (Figure 4G, Figure 5)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G and Figure 5.

claim: The data are most consistent with Model 1, the graded source-sink model of BMP/Chordin-mediated dorsal-ventral patterning during early zebrafish development.
source: Instead, our data are most consistent with Model 1, the graded source-sink model of BMP/Chordin-mediated dorsal-ventral patterning during early zebrafish development.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of all experimental data with model predictions.

claim: The conclusions are consistent with a recent complementary study.
source: Our conclusions are also consistent with a recent complementary study (Zinski et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: Shuttling models have gained prominence in many developmental contexts including scale-invariant patterning.
source: Notably, shuttling models (e.g. Model 5) have gained prominence in many developmental contexts including scale-invariant patterning (Ben-Zvi et al., 2008; Barkai and Ben-Zvi, 2009; Francois et al., 2009; Plouhinec and De Robertis, 2009; Ben-Zvi and Barkai, 2010; Ben-Zvi et al., 2011a; Haskel-Ittah et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: The fundamental tenet of shuttling models, whether putative shuttles such as Chordin change the diffusivity and distribution of signals such as BMP, has not been directly examined.
source: but the fundamental tenet, that is, whether putative shuttles such as Chordin change the diffusivity and distribution of signals such as BMP, has not been directly examined.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in previous research.

claim: Alternative models that do not invoke Chordin-dependent facilitated BMP diffusion can also explain scale-invariant patterning.
source: Alternative models that do not invoke Chordin-dependent facilitated BMP diffusion (Model 4) (Francois et al., 2009) or that postulate differential protein stability (Model 3) (Inomata et al., 2013) can also explain scale-invariant patterning.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The data do not provide strong evidence for shuttling of BMP2b at time scales relevant for dorsal-ventral patterning during early zebrafish embryogenesis.
source: Our data do not provide strong evidence for shuttling of BMP2b at time scales relevant for dorsal-ventral patterning during early zebrafish embryogenesis
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data.

claim: It is possible that other BMPs (e.g. BMP4, BMP7, ADMP) are shuttled by interactions with Chordin and its protease Tolloid/Xlr.
source: It is, however, possible that other BMPs (e.g. BMP4, BMP7, ADMP) are shuttled by interactions with Chordin and its protease Tolloid/Xlr.
evidence: This is speculation about possibilities not tested in the current study.

claim: tolloid mutants display a mild patterning defect of the ventral tail fin.
source: Indeed, tolloid mutants display a mild patterning defect of the ventral tail fin (Connors et al., 1999)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The ventral tail fin defect in tolloid mutants might reflect a requirement for the ventral accumulation of a weakly active, dorsally expressed BMP ligand such as ADMP.
source: that might reflect a requirement for the ventral accumulation of a weakly active, dorsally expressed BMP ligand such as ADMP (Dickmeis et al., 2001; Lele et al., 2001).
evidence: This is speculation supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The graded source-sink model (Model 1) describes a system in which the graded, ventrally biased distribution of bmp mRNA and the dorsally localized chd mRNA distribution produce opposing sources of extracellular, diffusing BMP and Chordin protein.
source: The graded source-sink model (Model 1) that is best supported by our data describes a system in which the graded, ventrally biased distribution of bmp mRNA and the dorsally localized chd mRNA distribution produce opposing sources of extracellular, diffusing BMP and Chordin protein, which together generate the BMP signaling gradient required for proper dorsal-ventral patterning.
evidence: This is a description of Model 1 based on the experimental findings.

claim: Model 1 fails to take other known dorsal-ventral regulators into account (e.g., ADMP, Sizzled, Follistatin, Noggin).
source: Notably, this model fails to take other known dorsal-ventral regulators into account (e.g., ADMP, Sizzled, Follistatin, Noggin).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of Model 1.

claim: Approximately one third of bmp2b and chordin mutant embryos can be rescued by apparently uniform bmp and chordin expression, respectively.
source: Furthermore, approximately one third of bmp2b and chordin mutant embryos can be rescued by apparently uniform bmp and chordin expression, respectively (Kishimoto et al., 1997; Fisher and Halpern, 1999) (Figure 3C)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies and data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The rescue of mutants by uniform expression argues against a strong requirement for concurrent opposing BMP and Chordin sources as long as one component of the system is biased.
source: arguing against a strong requirement for concurrent opposing BMP and Chordin sources as long as one component of the system is biased (i.e. ventrally biased bmp2b expression with uniform Chordin, or dorsally biased chordin expression with uniform BMP).
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue experiments.

claim: Further adjustments to the basic Model 1 will be required to fully describe dorsal-ventral patterning.
source: Thus, further adjustments to the basic Model 1 will be required to fully describe dorsal-ventral patterning.
evidence: This is inferred from the limitations of Model 1 discussed.

claim: The necessity of signal diffusion for developmental patterning has recently been challenged by several studies.
source: Although our results support a role for BMP diffusion in dorsal-ventral patterning, the necessity of signal diffusion for developmental patterning has recently been challenged by several studies (Brankatschk and Dickson, 2006; Roy and Kornberg, 2011; Alexandre et al., 2014; Dominici et al., 2017; Varadarajan et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent studies.
